newsitem.title: CHINA: China M2 seen rising 23 pct a year through 2000.
newsitem.headline: China M2 seen rising 23 pct a year through 2000.

text.p: China's broad M2 money supply is expected to rise by 23 percent a year through the year 2000, central bank governor Dai Xianglong told an economic forum on Tuesday.
M1, or currency in circulation plus current deposits, was expected to rise by 18 percent a year through 2000, said Dai, head of the People's Bank of China.
In July, China's M2 rose by 27 percent year-on-year while M1 rose by 15 percent.
China has set a target for M2 growth of 25 percent for all of 1996 and a target of 18 percent for M1.
